questions.q: What is metadata (or "payload") in the context of a vector database?
options: Structured data stored alongside a vector — like document type or date — that isn't part of the similarity calculation
A second, backup copy of the vector itself
The distance metric used to compare vectors
The name of the embedding model that produced the vector
questions.explain: Metadata rides along with a vector (called payload in Qdrant) but sits outside the similarity math — it's ordinary structured data used for filtering, not for computing closeness.

questions.q: What does a metadata-filtered query actually do?
options: It deletes every vector that doesn't match the filter
It finds the closest vectors to a query, restricted to only the vectors where given metadata conditions are also true
It re-embeds the query using different metadata
It ignores vector similarity entirely and sorts only by metadata
questions.explain: A filtered query combines nearest-neighbor search with exact-match or range conditions on metadata in the same request, returning only results that satisfy both.

questions.q: What is the main risk of post-filtering (searching first, then discarding non-matches)?
options: It always returns duplicate results
It cannot be combined with any distance metric
If the filter is restrictive, you can end up with fewer results than requested, or none, even if better matches exist deeper in the collection
It permanently deletes vectors that fail the filter
questions.explain: Post-filtering only filters within the initial candidate set the ANN search returned (say, the top 100); if most of those fail the filter, you may get far fewer than the requested number of results.

questions.q: How does pre-filtering differ from post-filtering?
options: It narrows to the vectors that pass the filter first, then searches for the closest among that smaller set
It filters only after the entire collection has been deleted and rebuilt
It is mathematically identical to post-filtering with no practical difference
It applies only to text data, never to images
questions.explain: Pre-filtering reverses the order: narrow to the matching subset first, then search within it — avoiding post-filtering's "too few results" problem, provided the filter is tightly integrated with the index.

questions.q: Why does the lesson call metadata filtering a safety requirement, not just a convenience, for a real RAG pipeline?
options: Because it makes embeddings smaller and cheaper to store
Because it is required by every embedding model's license
Because it increases the dimensionality of stored vectors
Scoping queries by tenant ID or access level keeps one user's or customer's documents from leaking into another's retrieved context
questions.explain: Filtering by tenant_id, access_level, or status (like excluding deprecated documents) is what prevents a RAG pipeline from retrieving and surfacing content a given user shouldn't see.
